_comment: FOLIO-ASSISTANT-CORE, declared as an INSTANTIATED harness. Owner, 2026-10-05, looking at the docs site's LHS navbar: 'do we have folio-assistant-core/ staging dir yet? if not, add it and instantaite it. i dont see it in list of harnesses...I would expect betwee who-iris and cat-harness for it to be there' (issue #2196, bean c5fm). The directory WAS staged -- `folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.json` exists and the root `folio-assistant.json` `needs` it -- but it was not INSTANTIATED: `harness-tiles.ts` computes `instantiated` from whether the instantiation root carries `<name>.config.json`, and `gen-navbar-include.ts` lists only instantiated harnesses under `Harnesses`. That is the owner's rule ('scan the root of the repo, look for <harness>.config.json as named instances'), the same rule and the same fix as `who-iris.config.json`. The position the owner expected is not hard-coded anywhere: who-iris `needs` folio-assistant-core and folio-assistant-core `needs` cat-harness, so the dependency walk that builds the navbar spine puts it between them.
_contentType_comment: `document`, matching `cat-harness.config.json` beneath it. This instance holds the content-model layer -- skills, processes, block kinds, adapters, schemas, glossary, methodologies -- as structured prose, data and code. It carries no Lean and no TeX of its own, so declaring `paper` would run the paper adapter's LaTeX-shaped QA axes over prose that never reaches pdflatex, which is the `critical`-on-prose failure `cat-harness.config.json` records.
